content.value_statement: Competitor ad research is difficult to organize across platforms and campaigns. This skill structures public ads into clear messaging, audience, format, and creative insights.
actual_capabilities: Guides research of public competitor ads across major ad libraries.
Organizes ad messaging by pain point, value proposition, audience, and call to action.
Compares themes, formats, and positioning across multiple competitors.
Identifies repeated creative and copy patterns in supplied ad evidence.
Produces structured recommendations for original campaign concepts.
Supports trend, platform, industry, and format comparisons.
limitations: The skill includes no browser automation, scraper, API client, or executable extraction script.
Results depend on ad library access and the completeness of supplied source material.
Ad frequency does not prove performance without spend, conversion, or engagement data.
Users must follow platform terms, privacy rules, and intellectual property requirements.

use_cases.title: Plan Original Campaigns
use_cases.description: Review competitor pain points and creative patterns before developing distinct campaign concepts.

use_cases.title: Map Market Positioning
use_cases.description: Compare how several brands describe value, audiences, and differentiation across public ads.

use_cases.title: Build Creative Briefs
use_cases.description: Turn observed formats, calls to action, and messaging gaps into evidence-based creative direction.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Competitor
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these current public ads from [competitor]. Summarize the main pain points, value propositions, audiences, formats, and calls to action.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of supplied ads from one company

prompt_templates.title: Compare Competitor Messaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the supplied ads from [company A], [company B], and [company C]. Identify shared themes, distinct positioning, and underserved messaging opportunities.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate positioning comparison across several brands

prompt_templates.title: Track Messaging Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these [competitor] ads from [period one] and [period two]. Explain changes in audience, pain points, offers, creative formats, and calls to action.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced analysis of campaign trends over time

prompt_templates.title: Develop a Campaign Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this competitor ad set, separate observations from assumptions, and create three original campaign directions for [brand], with evidence and testing hypotheses.

output_examples.input: Analyze six supplied ads from a project management competitor.
output_examples.output: The analysis groups ads into collaboration, meeting reduction, and documentation themes, then distinguishes observed copy from inferred audience intent.

output_examples.input: Compare public ads from three payroll platforms.
output_examples.output: The comparison highlights shared compliance claims, distinct audience segments, repeated calls to action, and two messaging gaps for further testing.

output_examples.input: Compare one competitor's first-quarter and second-quarter ad sets.
output: Second-quarter ads place greater emphasis on automation.
Video usage increased in the supplied sample.
Performance conclusions require engagement or conversion data.

best_practices: Provide source links, dates, platforms, and complete ad text for every item.
Separate direct observations from performance assumptions and strategic interpretations.
Use findings to create original campaigns that respect platform terms and intellectual property.
anti_patterns: Do not claim an ad performs well based only on frequency or continued availability.
Do not copy competitor headlines, designs, or protected creative assets.
Do not collect private data or bypass platform access controls.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically scrape ad libraries?
faq.answer: No. It provides a research and analysis workflow but includes no browser automation, API integration, or scraper.

faq.question: Which platforms can it analyze?
faq.answer: The guidance covers public libraries such as Facebook and LinkedIn and can support other platforms when you provide accessible ad evidence.

faq.question: Can it identify winning ads?
faq.answer: It can identify repeated patterns, but reliable performance conclusions require spend, engagement, conversion, or experiment data.

faq.question: What source material should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide screenshots, copy, calls to action, platform names, dates, source links, and any available performance context.

faq.question: Can I compare several competitors?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow supports comparisons of messaging, positioning, audience, format, and creative patterns across multiple brands.

faq.question: How should I use the findings legally?
faq.answer: Use public information for research, create original work, respect intellectual property, and follow platform terms and applicable laws.
